## 5. Systems Thinking and TQM Principles for DRRM Finance and Resources

The Executive Summary (section 1.2) identifies the pattern that ad-hoc fixes during events (borrowed supplies, event-by-event resolutions) relieve pressure faster than fundamental solutions and so keep the office improvising. In finance and logistics the fundamental solutions are known: a plan line before the event, a supplier agreement before the season, a stock level before the forecast. This chapter puts them in place and keeps them visible.

- **One chain from plan to proof** (Figure 6.2). LDRRMP target → LDRRMFIP line → AIP and budget → PPMP and APP → obligation → procurement → delivery → use → report → audit. A break anywhere shows up as unspent money or unsupported spending.

- **Speed through preparation.** The fastest emergency purchase is the one whose supplier, specification and price were agreed before the event; the fastest relief is the stock already in a safe warehouse.

- **Separation of duties.** The office that requests is not the office that certifies, pays, awards or holds the property. MODE records each step by position.

- **Feedback loops.** Quarterly utilisation, the STF ageing ledger, stock counts and COA observations feed the next LDRRMFIP and the next stock plan.

- **Prevention over correction.** The pre-audit checklist (Annex 6-B) prevents the most common COA findings: non-DRRM charges, QRF use without a declaration, missing utilisation reports, unliquidated advances, expired stocks and incomplete supporting documents.

## 6. LDRRMF Planning and Allocation

### 6.1 Computing the Fund

The LDRRMF is not less than 5% of **estimated revenue from regular sources** (RA 10121 Sec. 21). For a city this means the National Tax Allotment share plus regular local revenue (local taxes, fees and charges, and other recurring income), as defined by the Budget Office under DBM rules. It excludes one-time receipts, grants and borrowings.

The CY 2026 computation used the National Tax Allotment alone (Res. No. 05, s. 2025). The City Budget Office confirms the base each year on form FIN-F01 and keeps the computation with the budget. If the base was understated, the difference is appropriated through a supplemental budget or corrected in the next budget, as the Budget Office and the SP decide.

### 6.2 The 70/30 Split and the AA Line

**Table 6.5**

*Components of the LDRRMF*

| **Component**                                                                  | **Share**                   | **Use**                              | **Trigger**                                       |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Quick Response Fund                                                            | 30% of the LDRRMF           | Standby fund for relief and recovery | State of Calamity declared by the SP (JMC 2013-1) |
| Prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response, rehabilitation and recovery | 70% of the LDRRMF           | PPAs in the LDRRMFIP                 | Normal budget execution                           |
| – of which the anticipatory action line                                        | No more than 10% of the 70% | AA measures under RA 12287           | State of Imminent Disaster in force               |

**Worked example (illustration only, CY 2026 figures).** The 70% component is PHP 97,969,018.98, so the maximum AA line is PHP 9,796,901.90. For a hydrometeorological or geological hazard, at most PHP 2,939,070.57 (30%) may be disbursed for interventions more than 3 days before forecast impact, and up to PHP 6,857,831.33 (70%) for interventions within 3 days (Figure 6.4). The CY 2026 plan has no AA line, so these figures apply only once a plan includes one.

### 6.3 The LDRRMF Investment Plan

The LDRRMFIP is the annual plan that turns the LDRRMP into funded lines. Each line carries the LDRRMP and CDP PPA code; the thematic area (prevention and mitigation, preparedness, response, rehabilitation and recovery); the fund source (70%, QRF, STF by year of origin, other); the amount; the implementing office; the output and target; the procurement mode; and the quarter of implementation. Four lines are always shown on their own: the **AA line** (A4.6), the **EOC operations and maintenance line** (B7.5), **stock replenishment** for prepositioned relief items (A7.5), and **insurance premiums** for DRRM assets (A4.7).

### 6.4 Placement in the City Budget Calendar

**Table 6.6**

*Chapter 6 Actions in the City Budget Calendar*

| **Period**       | **Budget Calendar Event**                                                        | **Chapter 6 Action**                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| January–February | Prior-year closing; COA audit fieldwork                                          | STF ageing update (SOP 6-03); Q4 utilisation report (SOP 6-02); annual physical count of DRRM property and stocks (SOPs 6-10, 6-11)                                                           |
| March–May        | COA Annual Audit Report                                                          | Audit response plan (SOP 6-10); supplier list, specifications and stock levels refreshed before the typhoon season (SOPs 6-06, 6-11); inventory update with barangays and partners (SOP 6-12) |
| By mid-year      | Budget call; Local Finance Committee and Local Development Council deliberations | LDRRMFIP drafting (SOP 6-01); adequacy test (SOP 6-09)                                                                                                                                        |
| July–September   | CDRRMC approval; AIP finalised                                                   | LDRRMFIP approval; PPMP and APP                                                                                                                                                               |
| October–December | SP enacts the annual budget and adopts the LDRRMFIP                              | Insurance renewal check; framework agreements for the next year; pre-audit check (SOP 6-10)                                                                                                   |
| Every quarter    | CDRRMC quarterly meeting                                                         | Utilisation, stock and results report; Full Disclosure Policy posting                                                                                                                         |

*Note. Exact dates follow the Local Budget Calendar and the City Budget Office's budget call each year.*

## 7. Budget Execution, Utilisation and Disclosure

Execution follows the City's normal controls: allotment, obligation request certified by the Budget Officer, procurement, inspection and acceptance, disbursement voucher certified by the Accountant, and payment by the Treasurer. The CDRRMO keeps each LDRRMFIP line visible through every step.

**Table 6.7**

*Utilisation Measures Computed Each Quarter*

| **Measure**                      | **Formula**                                        | **Use**                                   |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Obligation rate                  | Obligations ÷ allotment for the year, by component | Shows whether plans are moving            |
| Disbursement rate                | Disbursements ÷ obligations, by component          | Shows whether deliveries are being paid   |
| PPA completion                   | Completed PPAs ÷ PPAs due by the quarter           | Shows results, not only spending          |
| Utilisation of the 70% component | Disbursements ÷ current-year 70% allotment         | IAT A4.4 target: at least 80% by year-end |

PPAs below plan by the end of the third quarter are flagged for realignment, with CDRRMC approval and SP concurrence where the law requires it. The quarterly report (FIN-F03, carried in MODE as BUD-F02) goes to the CDRRMC, is posted under the Full Disclosure Policy and feeds the Chapter 7 reporting calendar.

## 8. Special Trust Fund Management

Unexpended LDRRMF accrues to the STF and may be used only for DRRM within five years from the year it accrued; after that it reverts to the general fund (RA 10121 Sec. 21). The STF ledger (FIN-F04) keeps each balance by **year of origin** and shows its deadline, so the oldest money is programmed first. STF balances are also a lawful AA source under RA 12287 IRR Rule V Sec. 1(b), and they are not subject to the 30%/70% graduation.

Programming STF balances follows the same approvals as the 2024 and 2025 Trust Fund plans: CDRRMC approval, then SP adoption or concurrence on the City Accountant's advice (Res. No. 08, s. 2025). A bill to shorten the five-year period has been filed in Congress but is not law and is not applied.

## 9. Quick Response Fund

The QRF is a standby fund for relief and recovery in areas struck by a disaster. Under JMC 2013-1 it is used when the City is under a **State of Calamity** declared by the SP (Chapter 1, SOP GOV-04). COA has found LGUs using the QRF without that declaration; this chapter does not allow it. A State of Imminent Disaster under RA 12287 does not open the QRF: anticipatory action is funded from the AA line and other lawful sources (A4.6).

Unused QRF at year-end accrues to the STF. The QRF balance is reported in every quarterly report and after each use (FIN-F05). When QRF purchases replenish relief stocks, as in Res. No. 06, s. 2025, the items enter the stock card under SOP 6-11 like any other receipt.

## 10. Anticipatory Action Financing Under RA 12287

### 10.1 Sources and Their Rules

**Table 6.8**

*Sources of Anticipatory Action Funds*

| **Source**                                            | **Legal Basis**          | **30%/70% Graduation**                              | **Approval Route**                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| AA line in the LDRRMFIP (no more than 10% of the 70%) | IRR Rule V Sec. 1(b)     | Yes, for hydrometeorological and geological hazards | Released under the State of Imminent Disaster per the LDRRMFIP line |
| STF balances within their five-year period            | IRR Rule V Sec. 1(b)(i)  | No                                                  | CDRRMC programming; SP concurrence where required                   |
| Donations, partners, ODA, other LGUs                  | IRR Rule V Sec. 1(b)(ii) | No                                                  | Per donor terms and SP Res. No. 2024-102                            |
| NDRRM Fund augmentation                               | IRR Rule V Sec. 1(c)     | Per national rules                                  | Request through OCD; approval on NDRRMC recommendation              |

### 10.2 Release Rules

1.  Funds are released only while a State of Imminent Disaster declared by the City Mayor is in force (Chapter 1, SOP GOV-05), and only for AA measures in the approved PDRA. MODE's AA checklist is derived from the ten sections of IRR Rule IV; it is a working aid, not a list fixed by law.

2.  Disbursement is based on the anticipated extent of damage and disruption in the PDRA (Rule V Sec. 2).

3.  **Tranche rule** (hydrometeorological and geological hazards): disbursements for interventions to be carried out more than 3 days before forecast impact may not exceed 30% of the AA allocation; up to 70% may be disbursed for interventions within 3 days of impact (Figure 6.4).

4.  **Slow-onset hazards** (for example, drought): timelines and rates await the NDRRMC operational guidelines. Until then they are not graduated, but disbursements never exceed the year's AA allocation (ADR-025 item 4).

5.  **No Regrets Principle.** Goods bought for AA continue to reach the intended beneficiaries even if the hazard does not materialise (Rule V Sec. 3). Their distribution is recorded as for any other relief.

6.  Procurement, budget, accounting and audit rules still apply (Rule V Sec. 2). Where the procurement ground is "time is of the essence", the BAC records it under RA 12009 Sec. 35(b) (SOP 6-07).

7.  Unused AA funds accrue to the STF (Rule V Sec. 3).

8.  Third parties engaged for AA are paid on a *quantum meruit* basis from the AA allocation (Rule V Sec. 3).

**Figure 6.4**

*Anticipatory Action Allocation and the Tranche Rule, CY 2026 Illustration*

![Figure 83: Anticipatory Action Allocation and the Tranche Rule, CY 2026 Illustration](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-83.webp)

*Note. Computed from CDRRMC Res. No. 05, s. 2025 and RA 12287 IRR Rule V Sec. 2. Illustration only: the CY 2026 LDRRMFIP has no AA line, and the base may change once the Budget Office confirms the regular-revenue computation (A4.1). MODE applies the 30% and 70% limits from the aa_rules table (ADR-025).*

MODE applies the tranche and slow-onset rules from the aa_rules table, so a change in national guidelines is a parameter change, not a code change (ADR-025). Each disbursement is recorded against the declaration with its source, amount, purpose, intervention time and obligation reference, and MODE computes the lead time and tranche.

### 10.3 Getting the AA Line Into the Plan

The CY 2026 plan predates the IRR. Two routes are open, for the City to choose:

- **Amend the current or next-year LDRRMFIP** by CDRRMC resolution and SP action, realigning within the 70% component to create the AA line (precedent: Res. No. 08, s. 2025); or

- **Include it in the FY 2028 LDRRMFIP** at the next budget call, under CDP PPA 3.15.

Either way, the line names the AA measures it funds (by hazard and sector, from the contingency plans and the PDRA practice in Chapter 4), the implementing offices and the procurement mode for each item. Stocks to be prepositioned on an imminent threat (CDP PPA 1.1.7) are planned under section 13 so that the AA line buys what the warehouse cannot already supply.

## 11. Procurement for DRRM

### 11.1 Normal Procurement

DRRM goods, works and services follow the PPMP, the APP and competitive bidding or the appropriate alternative mode under RA 12009 and its IRR. The CDRRMO prepares the PPMP from the LDRRMFIP and writes the technical specifications; the BAC runs the procurement.

### 11.2 Pre-Arranged Supply

Before each typhoon season and at least once a year, the CDRRMO and the CGSO, with the BAC Secretariat, keep the following ready (SOP 6-06):

- a list of suppliers for relief goods, fuel, water, heavy equipment rental, transport, medicines and medical supplies, and generator service, with capacity and a contact position (FIN-F08);

- framework agreements under RA 12009 Sec. 16 and GPPB Circular No. 07-2026 where the BAC finds them suitable, stating item, maximum quantity, unit price or price basis, delivery time, call-off trigger and validity;

- standard specifications and price references for recurrent emergency items;

- agreements usable for anticipatory action, as RA 12287 IRR Rule IV contemplates (B6.6).

### 11.3 Emergency Procurement

Negotiated procurement – emergency cases (RA 12009 Sec. 35(b)) is used only when its ground exists: imminent danger to life or property during a State of Calamity, or time is of the essence because of a calamity and immediate action is needed to prevent loss of life or property or to restore vital public services, infrastructure or utilities. The requesting office writes the ground on FIN-F07 before the purchase, and the BAC and the HoPE confirm it under the RA 12009 IRR. Items are limited to what the emergency requires. Documentary requirements follow GPPB Circular No. 06-2026; posting and reporting follow the IRR and GPPB rules.

## 12. Donations and External Assistance

Donations in cash or in kind and external financial assistance are accepted, recorded and used as follows (SOP 6-08):

1.  One intake point per event, staffed by the CSWDO and the CGSO with the EOC Logistics or Finance and Administration desk.

2.  Acceptance follows SP Res. No. 2024-102 and COA rules; a deed of donation or acknowledgement receipt is issued (FIN-F09).

3.  Cash goes to the City Treasurer and is recorded by the City Accountant under COA Circular No. 2012-002 as a receipt from other sources, kept to its stated purpose.

4.  Goods are inspected, valued, recorded and stored by the CGSO (or the CSWDO for relief items), enter the stock card (SOP 6-11), and are issued against distribution records.

5.  Conditions set by the donor are respected; unsuitable goods are declined politely at intake.

6.  Donations used for AA are not subject to the 30%/70% graduation (IRR Rule V Sec. 2).

7.  Receipts, use and balances are disclosed with the quarterly report.

No personal data of beneficiaries is copied into the donations log; distribution lists stay with the CSWDO (RA 10173).

## 13. Resource Management and Prepositioned Stocks

Chapter 4 coordinates resources during an event: it receives requests, sets priorities and tracks each request from "requested" to "demobilised" (SOP 4-07). It can do so only if the resources exist, are known and can be released lawfully. This section sets how the City keeps relief stocks, warehouses and the resource inventory ready between events (Figure 6.5).

### 13.1 Stock Levels From Scenarios

Stock levels are set from the contingency plan scenarios (Chapter 3, SOP 3-06), not from habit. For each priority hazard the CSWDO and the CDRRMO take the number of families expected to be displaced in the most probable scenario, the number of days before national or provincial augmentation is expected, and the ration per family, and compute the level for each item (Annex 6-D). The NDRRMC Disaster Preparedness Minimum Standards set a floor of 500 food packs and 500 hygiene kits per LGU, each good for a family of five for three days; for a city of 85 barangays the scenario figure is likely to be higher, and the higher figure applies.

**Table 6.9**

*Parameters That Set Prepositioned Stock Levels*

| **Parameter**                | **Meaning**                                                                                                  | **Source**                                            |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| Families to be served        | Families expected in evacuation centres or home-based in the most probable scenario, by cluster of barangays | Contingency plans (CP Forms); CDRA exposure data      |
| Days of self-reliance        | Days the City must cover before augmentation arrives                                                         | Contingency plans; DSWD Field Office VIII agreements  |
| Ration per family per day    | Content of the food pack and non-food item kits                                                              | CSWDO standard pack; DPMS Vol. 2 minimum              |
| Target level                 | Families × days × ration, by item and by warehouse                                                           | Annex 6-D; approved by the CDRRMO Head with the CSWDO |
| Reorder point                | Level at which replenishment starts, allowing for procurement or call-off lead time                          | SOP 6-06 framework agreement delivery time            |
| Shelf life and rotation date | Expiry or best-before date and the date the item must be issued or replaced                                  | Supplier documents; stock card                        |

*Note. No fixed target is set in this chapter. The levels are computed and approved each year under SOP 6-11 and recorded in Annex 6-D.*

### 13.2 Warehousing, Rotation and Replenishment

- **Location.** Warehouses stand in low-risk areas (DPMS Vol. 2), checked against the hazard maps in Chapter 3, and are spread so that one flooded road does not cut off all stocks. The 10-Year Plan's seven planned storage facilities are sited using the same check.

- **Condition.** Dry, secure, ventilated and pest-controlled; stock on pallets; a fire extinguisher and a posted layout; access controlled by the custodian.

- **Rotation.** First expiry, first out. Items within the rotation window are issued to regular CSWDO programmes, feeding programmes or drills before they expire, so nothing is wasted.

- **Replenishment.** When the stock of an item reaches its reorder point, the custodian raises a replenishment request against the stock replenishment line, the AA line (on an imminent threat) or the QRF (under a State of Calamity), whichever window is open.

- **Count.** A monthly spot count by the custodian and an annual physical count with the CGSO and the COA schedule; variances are explained in writing.

**Figure 6.5**

*Prepositioned Stock Cycle*

![Figure 84: Prepositioned Stock Cycle](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-84.webp)

*Note. Prepared for this chapter. The two shaded boxes are the decisions that keep stocks adequate. The same item carries one record across the stock card and the MODE resource list.*

### 13.3 The DRRM Resource Inventory

The EOC needs one view of what can be mobilised, whoever owns it (B6.3). The DRRM resource inventory therefore covers four holders: City offices; barangays (BDRRMC equipment and stocks); partners (national agencies, neighbouring LGUs under mutual aid, CSOs); and suppliers and private-sector providers under signed commitments (B6.6). City-owned items are copied from the property records; others are recorded with the agreement that commits them, the contact position, the activation trigger and the date last confirmed. An entry that has not been confirmed in the last twelve months is shown as unconfirmed.

In MODE, the resources table holds each item with category, unit, quantity, owner office, location and serviceability, and resource requests in Chapter 4 link to it. The current schema has no fields for holder type, commitment reference, reorder point or expiry date. Until they are added, these are kept on the LOG forms (section 20) and noted in the resource record; the gap is listed in section 19 for the platform custodian.

### 13.4 Equipment Readiness

Response equipment and vehicles are inventoried, serviceable and on a preventive maintenance schedule (A8.3). The CDRRMO keeps the schedule and the maintenance log for DRRM equipment; serviceability is updated in the inventory after each check, so the EOC does not count equipment that cannot be used. Equipment out of service for more than one operational period is reported to the CDRRMO Head with the repair plan.

## 14. Property and Asset Accountability

DRRM property bought with the LDRRMF, STF, QRF, AA funds or donations is government property. The CGSO records it, issues it to the end user on a Property Acknowledgement Receipt or Inventory Custodian Slip, and includes it in the annual physical count. The CDRRMO:

- keeps a DRRM asset register linked to the MODE resource inventory, so the same item has one record;

- returns or transfers property on reassignment or separation of the accountable person;

- reports loss or damage at once, with the incident record, for relief from accountability under COA rules;

- applies the same rules to equipment lent to barangays, with a signed receipt and a return date.

Consumables issued in an emergency (fuel, food packs, non-food items) are supported by issue slips, trip tickets and distribution summaries. The CDRRMO file holds aggregate distribution counts only; named lists stay with the CSWDO.

## 15. Risk Financing and Insurance

The City layers its risk finance (Figure 6.6): the QRF and the 70% component for frequent, smaller events; the AA line, the STF and pre-arranged supply for imminent events; insurance for damage to public assets; and national funds, contingent credit and partners for catastrophic events. SOP 6-09 tests that layering each year against a severe credible scenario (a Thelma-type flash flood; a Yolanda-strength typhoon) and records the shortfall and the fallback sources.

**Figure 6.6**

*Risk Layering of DRRM Finance*

![Figure 85: Risk Layering of DRRM Finance](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-85.webp)

*Note. Prepared for this chapter after the UNDRR Disaster Resilience Scorecard, Essential 3, and the Disaster Rehabilitation and Recovery Planning Guide (NEDA, 2020).*

The CDRA reports that only 15% of critical point facilities are insured and no lifeline utility is insured. Under RA 656, public property is insured with the GSIS. CDP PPAs 1.3 and 1.2.3 programme insurance of buildings, equipment and early warning devices. The EOC, evacuation centres, DRRM warehouses and DRRM equipment are listed first.

## 16. Standard Operating Procedures

Each SOP has a control block and a step table. Every step states the actor (a position or office, never a person), the action and decision rule, inputs and outputs, and timing, control and escalation. Form codes are those of section 20. In MODE, each SOP runs as a workflow (a multi-office management cycle) or a protocol (a point-of-action checklist) that carries the same steps.

<p>Out: SP resolution or ordinance</p></th>

<p>Out: Controlled LDRRMFIP in MODE</p></th>

<p>Control: Second person checks the load</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMO Head</p></th>
</tr>

**Minimum records:** FIN-F01; FIN-F02; PPMP; LFC/LDC minutes; CDRRMC resolution; SP act; controlled LDRRMFIP in MODE.

### SOP 6-05 \| Anticipatory Action Funding and Disbursement Under a State of Imminent Disaster
**Process owner:** CDRRMO Head with the City Budget Office, City Accountant, City Treasurer and BAC. **Purpose:** Release AA funds immediately and lawfully once a State of Imminent Disaster is declared, within the 10% ceiling and the tranche rule, and account for them in the 45-day report.

**SOP 6-05 Control Block**

| Process owner (operational) | CDRRMO Head; EOC Finance and Administration desk                                                                          |
| Trigger                     | Mayor's declaration of a State of Imminent Disaster; a revised impact forecast during the declaration                     |
| Forms                       | FIN-F06; FIN-F07; FIN-F09 (donations); LOG-F01                                                                            |
| IAT v1.7 indicators         | A4.6 (0, High); A10.8 (0, High); B6.6 (1, Medium)                                                                         |
| Functional MR links         | MR-08; MR-16; MR-07                                                                                                       |
| Policy basis                | RA 12287 Secs. 6–7; IRR Rule IV; Rule V Secs. 1–3; Rule VI Sec. 1; RA 12009 Sec. 35(b)                                    |
| Cross-references            | SOP GOV-05 (PR-SOID-REQUEST, PR-LIFT-REPORT); Chapter 4 PDRA and AA execution; SOPs 6-07, 6-11; Chapter 7 (45-day report) |

**Table 6.19**

**SOP 6-05 Steps and Controls**

<th><p>In: LDRRMFIP; FIN-F04</p>
<p>Out: FIN-F06 envelope</p></th>

<p>Control: FIN-F07 where used</p>

## 17. Responsibility Assignment (RACI)

| **\[R\] Responsible** | **\[A\] Accountable** | **\[C\] Consulted** | **\[I\] Informed** |
|-----------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|--------------------|

"A" is the single proposed process-accountable owner; "R" performs; "C" is consulted; "I" is informed. The RACI allocates work; it does not transfer the legal powers named in section 3.

*Note. MY = City Mayor (HoPE for awards); SP = Sangguniang Panlungsod; CC = CDRRMC; HD = CDRRMO Head; RP = CDRRMO Research and Planning Division; AT = CDRRMO Administration and Training Division; BU = City Budget Office; AC = City Accountant; TR = City Treasurer; BA = BAC; GS = CGSO; SW = CSWDO. Where a row has two "A" entries, each holds a distinct legal act: the CDRRMC approves and the SP adopts or concurs (LDRRMFIP, STF); the SP declares a State of Calamity and the Mayor approves QRF spending; the Mayor declares a State of Imminent Disaster and approves AA spending; the CDRRMO Head approves the stock plan and the CSWDO holds custody of relief goods; the CDRRMO Head runs the adequacy test and the SP appropriates premiums.*

Corrective actions record the finding, evidence, cause, action, accountable office, due date and verification, and go into the corrective and preventive action register run under Chapter 7 (Chapter 1, section 9.5).

**Legal readings to confirm with the City Legal Office and OCD VIII before adoption:**

1.  Whether the AA line may be created in the current year by realignment within the 70% component, or only in a new LDRRMFIP.

2.  Whether "allocation for anticipatory action" in Rule V Sec. 2 means the year's AA line or the amount released for one declaration.

3.  The treatment of slow-onset hazards until the NDRRMC operational guidelines are issued (ADR-025 item 4).

4.  Whether "time is of the essence" under RA 12009 Sec. 35(b) covers AA purchases under a State of Imminent Disaster when no State of Calamity is in force.

5.  The exact composition of "estimated revenue from regular sources" for the City (A4.1).

6.  Whether stock replenishment bought from the AA line for an imminent threat, and not used because the hazard did not occur, is carried as AA-funded stock or transferred to the regular stock line.

## 22. Concluding Notes

The City already sets aside and approves its DRRM fund, and it has bought relief goods quickly when a State of Calamity allowed. The work now is to make funds and supplies reachable at the right moment and to prove what they did: an anticipatory action line before impact, a QRF under its proper trigger after impact, suppliers agreed and stocks set before the season, an inventory the EOC can trust, and records that tell the CDRRMC, the public and COA what each peso and each item did.

Writing these procedures does not implement them. Until the AA line exists, the first stock plan is approved, the inventory reaches the barangays and suppliers, and at least one exercise has tested SOPs 6-04, 6-05 and 6-11 with the Budget, Accounting, Treasury, BAC, CGSO and CSWDO offices, this chapter remains a controlled working draft.

## Annex 6-C. Anticipatory Action Funding Pathway and Tranche Worksheet

Basis: RA 12287 and its IRR (signed 14 September 2026), Rule V Secs. 1–3; ADR-025. The official text governs. DBM–COA guidelines on AA funds and NDRRMC operational guidelines are pending; this worksheet will be revised when they are issued.

1.  **Plan.** The LDRRMFIP carries an AA line of no more than 10% of the 70% component, naming the AA measures (by hazard and sector), lead offices and procurement mode (SOP 6-01).

2.  **Pre-arrange.** Framework agreements, supplier lists and stock plans cover AA items (SOPs 6-06, 6-11).

3.  **Declare.** The City Mayor declares a State of Imminent Disaster after the PDRA, CDRRMC recommendation and RDRRMC process (Chapter 1, SOP GOV-05).

4.  **Release.** Budget, Accounting and Treasury release funds immediately, within the tranche rule (SOP 6-05).

5.  **Deliver.** Lead offices carry out AA measures; the No Regrets Principle applies.

6.  **Lift and report.** The declaration lifts on hazard occurrence or on the Mayor's lifting; unused AA funds accrue to the STF; the 45-day report includes AA fund use (Chapter 7).

## 1. Introduction and Assessment-Informed Rationale

Chapters 1 to 6 set what the City does before, during and after a disaster and how it pays for it. This chapter asks whether those things are being done, whether they work, and what changes as a result. It is the "Check" and "Act" of the Plan–Do–Check–Act cycle that Chapter 1 (section 9) adopts for the whole Manual.

A procedure that is written but never measured drifts. The Executive Summary (section 1.2) names the risk of drifting goals: with Mandatory compliance at 32.9%, the working standard can settle at "we responded" rather than "we met the standard". The remedy is a fixed standard, measured the same way every year, with gaps tracked to closure and lessons fed back into plans and the Manual. This chapter supplies those mechanisms.

The IAT v1.7 baseline shows that the City plans and reports, but rarely closes the loop (Figure 7.1). Domain A10 (Partnerships, M&E and Accountability) has an index of **1.86 (Developing)**, with 1 of 4 Mandatory items compliant. Regular reporting to OCD Region VIII and the DILG is in place (A10.3 at 3). The gaps are in the learning loop: no 45-day post-declaration report template (A10.8, score 0, High); no annual M&E report of the LDRRMP (A10.4); after-action reviews that rest on the FGD alone (A10.6, B7.4); no disaster event and loss database (A5.4, score 0); and data-protection arrangements for DRRM data not sighted (A5.5) (Table 7.1).

### 1.1 What the Records Show

- **A results-based M&E design exists.** The DRRM 10-Year Plan 2023–2032 (Chapter 5 of the plan) bases its monitoring on the UNDRR Ten Essentials for Making Cities Resilient, overlaid with NDRRMP 2020–2030 outcomes, the DILG capacity development pillars, the Sendai Framework targets and the Regional Development Plan of Region VIII (Figure 7.3). It sets a monitoring tool (Form 5D) and five outputs, including an annual progress report each January, a physical and financial report each December and a mid-term report in 2029, reported to the CDRRMC and the Local Development Council.

- **Mandates to monitor exist.** RA 10121 Sec. 11(b) tasks the CDRRMC to approve, monitor and evaluate the LDRRMP and to review and test it regularly. EO 2024-032A Sec. 2(a) repeats the task. EO 2022-00020 created the CDRRMP Technical Working Group for formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating the plan, with thematic focal offices: CENRO for prevention and mitigation, the DILG City Office for preparedness, the CSWDO for response and the CPDO for recovery. EO 2023-0026 tasks the Project TRANSFORM TWG to monitor indicators in the NRC resilience scorecard.

- **The loop is not yet closed.** No annual results report and no baseline database were found in the document set. The plan itself observes that the City's performance has been assessed mainly through national award systems, without outcome-based M&E linked to sector results.

- **Event history is scattered.** The 10-Year Plan lists the six most significant disasters; the CDRA lists previous disasters with damage figures; RDANA and PDNA reports exist for 2017 to 2021. The CDRA recommends a disaster event and loss database. Chapter 5 found one damage figure in the plan that is not plausible (Yolanda), which a controlled database would have caught.

- **The assessment itself is the first full baseline.** The October–November 2026 IAT cycle scored 140 indicators, applied the evidence rule and produced the first Institutional Maturity Index (IMI 1.98). The validation workshop of 1–4 December 2026 will confirm or revise each score. That cycle is the model for the annual cycles this chapter sets.

### 1.2 Design Considerations

1.  **Measure the same way every year.** The IAT, the LDRRMP indicators and the reporting calendar stay stable so that change can be seen; when the instrument changes, the change is versioned and the old results stay readable.

2.  **Evidence before score.** A score of 3 needs an approved document and proof of use; interviews and FGDs alone cap at 2. The same rule applies to M&E claims: an output is "done" only with its means of verification.

3.  **One register.** Findings from the IAT, AARs, exercises, audits, compliance reports and feedback go into one corrective and preventive action (CAPA) register, defined in Chapter 1 (section 9.5, GOV-10) and run under this chapter.

4.  **Closure means effective.** An action is closed when the problem it addressed has not recurred in the next test, exercise or event, not when work has started.

5.  **Separate the scorer from the validator.** Whoever scores an indicator does not validate it; MODE enforces this in the database (ADR-029).

6.  **Privacy by design.** M&E and knowledge products use aggregate counts; personal data stays with the office that collected it, under the Data Privacy Act.

## 2. Purpose and Intended Results

This chapter sets how the City monitors and evaluates its DRRM plan and its DRRM institutions, how it learns from events and exercises, how it tracks corrective action to closure, how it meets its reporting duties, and how it keeps and shares DRRM knowledge and data safely.

Intended results:

1.  The LDRRMP has an approved indicator set with baselines, and the CDRRMC receives an annual results report each January (A10.4).

2.  The IAT is applied every year with the same instrument, evidence rules and separation of duties, and its results feed the action plan and the Manual (MR-12 to MR-15).

3.  Every EOC activation at Blue or Red, every State of Calamity or State of Imminent Disaster, and every exercise is followed by an after-action review whose findings are tracked (A10.6, B7.4).

4.  Every corrective action in the CAPA register has an owner, a due date and verification evidence, and is closed only when shown to be effective.

5.  The 45-day post-declaration report is submitted on time after each State of Imminent Disaster (A10.8), and all other mandated reports follow a calendar.

6.  A disaster event and loss database holds the City's history from 1991 onwards in a standard format (A5.4).

7.  Lessons from Ormoc's own events and from other LGUs and networks are recorded with the changes they produced (A10.9).

8.  DRRM data handling meets the Data Privacy Act: a designated DPO, privacy notices, data-sharing agreements and a breach procedure (A5.5).

## 3. Scope, Application and Institutional Boundaries

**In scope:** monitoring and evaluation of the LDRRMP and of the CDRRMO and EOC; the annual IAT cycle; after-action reviews and exercise evaluation; the CAPA register; compliance and post-declaration reporting; the disaster event and loss database; records, lessons and peer learning; protection of DRRM data; management review and performance reporting.

## 5. Systems Thinking and the Learning Cycle

The CDRRMO learns in two ways. In single-loop learning it corrects how a procedure was carried out: a SitRep was late, so the cut-off reminder is moved earlier. In double-loop learning it questions the procedure or its assumptions: SitReps are late because the same staff run the EOC and the field, so the roster changes (Argyris and Schön, 1978). The IAT and the AAR find problems of both kinds; the CAPA register records which kind each action is, so that repeated single-loop fixes to the same problem trigger a deeper review.

**Figure 7.2 shows the learning system. Evidence arrives from five sources: the annual IAT cycle, LDRRMP monitoring, after-action reviews and exercises, audits and compliance reports, and feedback and peer learning. One register turns it into change in plans, the Manual, MODE and people's capacity. The next cycle measures again, which is how effectiveness is verified.**

**Figure 7.2**

*The City DRRM Learning System*

![Figure 87: 5. Systems Thinking and the Learning Cycle](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-87.webp)

*Note. Prepared for this chapter from the PDCA cycle in Chapter 1 (section 9.2) and the CAPA requirements in Chapter 1 (section 9.5).*

- **Against drifting goals.** Standards are set by the IAT rubric and the law, not by last year's performance. The register shows Mandatory gaps first.

- **Against shifting the burden.** An AAR finding that recurs in two events is escalated from a single-loop fix to a CDRRMC decision on the fundamental solution (staffing, issuance, budget).

- **Delays are named.** Each action states when its effect can be seen (the next drill, the next season, the next IAT cycle), so the CDRRMC does not abandon a correct fix before it has had time to work.

## 6. Monitoring and Evaluation of the LDRRMP

### 6.1 The Integrated M&E Design

The City already adopted the design in its 10-Year Plan (Figure 7.3). This chapter does not replace it; it operates it. The UNDRR Ten Essentials are the base. The NDRRMP outcomes, the DILG capacity pillars, the Sendai targets and the Regional Development Plan of Region VIII are overlays that align local indicators with national and regional reporting. This Manual adds one layer: the IAT Institutional Maturity Index as the measure of the CDRRMO and the EOC themselves.

**Figure 7.3**

Each indicator is recorded on the M&E matrix (ME-F01, aligned with the plan's Form 5D): result level (output, outcome, impact), indicator and definition, unit, baseline value and year, target by year, data source, collection method and frequency, responsible office, and the Ten Essentials, NDRRMP, Sendai and IAT codes it maps to. | Outcome           | Change in institutions, systems and behaviour that the PPAs aim for | IAT IMI and Mandatory compliance; share of barangays with functional BDRRMCs; share of families reached by warnings who took protective action; share of recovery PPAs completed to BBB standards    |

### 6.4 Data Quality

Each value carries its source, date and the office that supplied it. A blank means "not reported" and is never entered as zero. Barangay figures use the 85-barangay PSGC list (Chapter 3). Values that change by more than half from the previous year are checked with the source office before publication. The M&E unit keeps the calculation for each composite indicator so that another person can repeat it.

## 7. The Institutional Assessment Cycle

The IAT measures the CDRRMO and the EOC themselves. The Introduction (sections 5.1 to 5.3) describes the instrument and the baseline. This section sets how it is used every year.

### 7.1 The Instrument

IAT v1.7 has 140 indicators in 22 domains: Part A (CDRRMO), 82 indicators in 10 domains; Part B (EOC), 43 indicators in 7 domains; Part C (interface with other City offices and partners), 15 indicators in 5 domains. Parts A and B have 79 Mandatory and 46 Good Practice indicators and form the Institutional Maturity Index (IMI). Part C names a lead office other than the CDRRMO and is reported as a separate Interface Index, never added to the IMI. The 108-indicator sheet in the City's earlier statement of design principles is IAT v1.0, which the Vault records as superseded.

### 7.2 Scoring and Evidence Rules

**Table 7.7**

*IAT Scoring Rubric and Evidence Rule*

| **Score** | **Level**      | **Meaning and Minimum Evidence**                                                                     |
|-----------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0         | Absent         | Nothing exists.                                                                                      |
| 1         | Initial        | Exists verbally or informally only.                                                                  |
| 2         | Developing     | A draft or partial arrangement exists. The maximum for a score supported only by interviews or FGDs. |
| 3         | Compliant      | An approved document exists and there is proof of use.                                               |
| 4         | Advanced       | Level 3 plus a test, exercise or AAR showing improvement.                                            |
| NA        | Not applicable | Only with a written justification.                                                                   |

*Note. From the IAT v1.7 Scoring_Lookups sheet and Methodology v1.1, section 5.2. Until validation, the lower score stands.*

**Table 7.8**

*IAT Indices and Priority Formulas*

| **Measure**                  | **Formula and Rule**                                                                                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Domain or part index         | Σ(score × weight) ÷ Σ(weight) over scored items. Bands: below 0.5 Absent; 0.5–1.49 Initial; 1.5–2.49 Developing; 2.5–3.49 Compliant; 3.5 and above Advanced. The unrounded value is banded. |
| Institutional Maturity Index | The index over all scored items in Parts A and B.                                                                                                                                           |
| Mandatory compliance         | Scored Mandatory items at 3 or 4 ÷ scored Mandatory items. A domain is "Compliant" only at 100%.                                                                                            |
| Interface Index              | The index over Part C, reported separately.                                                                                                                                                 |
| Gap priority                 | (4 − score) × weight × 1.5 for Mandatory items; × 1.0 for Good Practice and all Part C items. High 9 and above; Medium 4 to 8.9; Low below 4.                                               |

*Note. The scoring rules are held once in SQL in MODE and mirrored in the application code under a parity test (ADR-005); a change to a formula is a change to the controlled instrument and needs a new IAT version.*

### 7.3 Validation and Separation of Duties

Every score is validated before the results are final. MODE records who set each score; a validation by the same person is refused. A validator either confirms the score or revises it; a revision needs a written note, and the submitted score is kept. Baseline rows loaded from the workbook have no recorded scorer, so the lead assessor does not validate them (ADR-029; Methodology v1.1, section 6.1). The agreement rate between scorers and validators is reported as a calibration signal, not as a performance measure of individuals.

### 7.4 The Annual Cycle

**Figure 7.4 shows the cycle. MODE carries each cycle through five statuses: draft, fieldwork, validation, final and archived. A final cycle is not edited; corrections are made in the next cycle. The proposed timing places fieldwork and validation in the third and fourth quarters, so the results reach the January annual report and the budget call that follows.**

**Figure 7.4**

*The Annual IAT Cycle*

![Figure 89: 7.4 The Annual Cycle](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-89.webp)

*Note. Prepared for this chapter from the MODE assessment_cycles statuses, ADR-005, ADR-029 and Methodology v1.1. The timing in the reporting calendar (Figure 7.6) is a proposal for CDRRMC decision.*

### 7.5 From Gap to Action to Manual

Each gap routes to an improvement action with a responsible office, target date and budget source, and to the Manual section that addresses it (MR-14). MODE holds actions per indicator and cycle with a status (not started, ongoing, done, dropped) and shows the chain from indicator to master requirement to Manual document in the traceability view. Actions arising from the IAT are copied into the CAPA register so that one register holds all corrective work.

> PLATFORM NOTE. The MODE actions table has no fields for root cause, verification evidence or effectiveness review, which Chapter 1 (Table 1.23) requires of a CAPA entry. Until they are added, the CAPA register is kept on ME-F05 and the MODE action carries the ME-F05 reference. The gap is listed in section 17.

## 8. After-Action Reviews and Exercise Evaluation

An after-action review asks four questions: what was supposed to happen; what actually happened; why there was a difference; and what will be done about it. It examines systems and decisions, not individuals. Figure 7.5 shows the path from trigger to closure.

**Table 7.9**

*Events That Require an After-Action Review*

| **Trigger**                                                          | **Minimum Form**                                                                   | **Proposed Timing**                                 |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| EOC activation at Blue or Red                                        | Hot wash at deactivation (Chapter 4, SOP 4-09) and a full AAR (ME-F03)             | Hot wash on deactivation; AAR report within 30 days |
| State of Calamity or State of Imminent Disaster                      | Full AAR; for a State of Imminent Disaster, linked to the 45-day report (SOP 7-06) | Within 30 days of lifting                           |
| Functional or full-scale exercise                                    | Exercise evaluation (ME-F04)                                                       | Within 15 days of the exercise                      |
| Tabletop exercise or drill                                           | Short evaluation (ME-F04, short form)                                              | Within 7 days                                       |
| Near miss or significant procedural failure, even without activation | Focused AAR (ME-F03, focused form)                                                 | Within 15 days of discovery                         |

*Note. The timings are proposals of this chapter for CDRRMC adoption; they are not set by national rules.*

**Figure 7.5**

*From After-Action Review to Verified Closure*

![Figure 90: From After-Action Review to Verified Closure](/library/moo-consolidated/fig-90.webp)

*Note. Prepared for this chapter. ER-F06 is the Chapter 4 after-action and corrective action record; ME-F05 is the CAPA register entry.*

**Who takes part.** The EOC Manager, section chiefs, the Incident Commander or a representative, sector offices and barangays involved, and, where possible, community representatives and partners. A facilitator who did not hold a command role leads. Participants are told that the AAR is blame-free and that its record names positions, not people.

**What is recorded.** The timeline from the official warning products and the logbook; decisions and their basis; what worked; what did not, with evidence; root or contributing causes; and recommended actions. Annex 7-C gives the report outline. Exercise evaluations follow the exercise objectives and the EOC Capability Assessment Checklist where it applies.

## 9. Corrective and Preventive Action Management

Chapter 1 (section 9.5) defines the CAPA register and its fields; SOP GOV-10 names it. This chapter operates it (SOP 7-05). Every source in Figure 7.2 feeds it: IAT gaps, AAR and exercise findings, COA observations (Chapter 6, FIN-F11), compliance report gaps, recovery monitoring (Chapter 5), stakeholder feedback and changes in law.

**Table 7.10**

*CAPA Status Rules*

| **Status**         | **Meaning**                                                                              | **Who May Set It**                              |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Open               | Entered with problem statement, source and risk consequence; owner and due date proposed | M&E unit                                        |
| Planned            | Root cause, action, owner, due date and resources agreed                                 | Accountable owner, confirmed by the CDRRMO Head |
| In progress        | Work has started                                                                         | Accountable owner                               |
| Implemented        | Evidence of completion attached                                                          | Accountable owner                               |
| Closed – effective | The problem has not recurred in the next test, exercise, event or IAT cycle              | CDRRMO Head; the CDRRMC for High-priority items |
| Reopened           | The problem recurred; a new cause analysis is required                                   | M&E unit                                        |
| Escalated          | Overdue twice, or beyond the CDRRMO's authority                                          | CDRRMO Head to the CDRRMC                       |

*Note. An action is never closed because it has started (Chapter 1, section 9.5). Priority follows the IAT gap-priority bands where the source is an IAT indicator; otherwise the CDRRMO Head assigns High, Medium or Low by life-safety and legal consequence.*

## 11. Knowledge Management

### 11.1 Disaster Event and Loss Database

The City needs one record of every disaster that affected it: what happened, where, to whom and at what cost (A5.4). The database uses the Sendai Framework and DesInventar fields (Annex 7-E), records barangay as the smallest unit using PSGC codes, and holds aggregate counts only. It starts with the events already documented (the 1991 flash flood, Yolanda in 2013, the 2017 earthquake, Urduja in 2017, Ursula in 2019 and Odette in 2021) and is updated after every event from the RDANA, DROMIC, PDNA and final SitRep. Each figure carries its source; implausible figures, such as the Yolanda damage printed in the 10-Year Plan, are flagged until verified (SOP 7-07).

### 11.2 Records and the Vault

DRRM records follow Chapter 1 (GOV-08). Issuances, plans, reports and evidence are kept in the MODE Vault; documents are superseded, never deleted, and each has an owner office and a date. Retention and disposal follow the schedules approved under RA 9470; nothing is disposed of by the CDRRMO on its own. Evidence files attached to IAT scores identify sources by office or position, never by an informant's name (MR-15).

### 11.3 Lessons Register and Manual Revision

A lesson is recorded only when it changed something or when a change has been proposed. The lessons register (ME-F08) links each lesson to its source (AAR, exercise, IAT, peer exchange), the change made (plan, Manual section, form, training, MODE rule) and the CAPA entry. Changes to the Manual are made as new versions in the MODE Library; approved versions are never edited, and only the CDRRMO Head approves a version.

### 11.4 Peer Learning

Ormoc takes part in several networks: the Making Cities Resilient 2030 initiative, the National Resilience Council Resilient LGU programme (SP Res. No. 2021-036), the EDC Adopt-a-City partnership and DENR–EDC Project TRANSFORM (EO 2023-0026), and OCD forums. Each exchange is recorded with what was learned and what the City changed as a result (A10.9). Partnerships themselves are managed under Chapter 8.

## 12. Protection of DRRM Data

DRRM work collects personal data: evacuee and beneficiary lists, casualty lists, contact rosters, volunteer records. The Data Privacy Act applies in full, including during emergencies. MODE is designed to hold aggregate counts only for affected populations; named lists stay with the office that collected them (CSWDO, CHO) and are shared only under a data-sharing agreement or as the law allows.

**Table 7.12**

*Data Protection Controls for DRRM Information*

| **Control**             | **Requirement**                                                                                                                             | **Owner**                           |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Data Protection Officer | The City DPO is designated and covers DRRM processing; a CDRRMO compliance officer for privacy is named.                                    | City Administrator; CDRRMO Head     |
| Privacy notices         | Short notices on registration, evacuation and relief forms state purpose, sharing and retention.                                            | CSWDO; CDRRMO                       |
| Data-sharing agreements | Signed with the CSWDO, CHO, CPDO and partners that exchange personal data with the CDRRMO.                                                  | City Legal Office; DPO              |
| Aggregate rule          | Reports, SitReps, the event database and M&E products use counts; blanks are "not reported".                                                | M&E unit; EOC                       |
| Small counts            | Where a count in a sex-, age- or disability-disaggregated table could identify a person, the DPO decides whether to suppress or combine it. | DPO                                 |
| Security                | Role-based access; encryption in transit; access logs; shared-device sign-out (MODE ADR-004, ADR-014); NPC Circular No. 2023-06.            | City ICT office; platform custodian |
| Breach response         | Contain, assess and, where required, notify the NPC and affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowledge (NPC Circular No. 16-03).       | DPO; CDRRMO Head                    |

> VALIDATION NOTE. The DPO designation, privacy notices and data-sharing agreements were not sighted in the document set (A5.5). The CPDO and the City Administrator's Office are to confirm the current arrangements at the workshop.

<th>M&amp;E unit with CPDO</th>
<th><p>Check consistency of results and PPAs with the AIP and CDP (Memo No. 147, s. 2017).</p>
<p>Decision: Any PPA without an AIP line or vice versa?</p></th>
<th><p>In: AIP; CDP</p>
<p>Out: Consistency note</p></th>
<th><p>Time: With step 4</p>
<p>Control: Note attached to ME-F02</p>
<p>Escalate: CPDO Head</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th>6. Present</th>
<th>CDRRMO Head</th>
<th><p>Present the annual report to the CDRRMC and the LDC.</p>
<p>Decision: Accepted? Decisions on off-track results?</p></th>
<th><p>In: ME-F02</p>
<p>Out: CDRRMC resolution; LDC minutes</p></th>
<th><p>Time: January meeting</p>
<p>Control: Decisions entered as CAPA items</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMC Chair</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th>7. Publish and file</th>
<th>M&amp;E unit</th>
<th><p>Post the summary report; file the full report and data in the Vault.</p>
<p>Decision: Posted?</p></th>
<th><p>In: Approved report</p>
<p>Out: Posting proof; Vault entry</p></th>
<th><p>Time: Within 15 days of approval</p>
<p>Control: No personal data in published products</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMO Head</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
</tbody>
</table>

**Minimum records:** ME-F01 matrix; data call; checked dataset and query log; ME-F02 report; consistency note; CDRRMC resolution; posting proof.

**Process owner:** CDRRMO Research and Planning, with designated assessors. **Purpose:** Score all 140 IAT indicators each year with the same instrument and evidence rules, so that change in the CDRRMO and EOC can be measured.

**SOP 7-02 Steps and Controls**

<p>Escalate: CDRRMO Head</p></th>

**SOP 7-03 Steps and Controls**

<th><p>Time: Within 20 days</p>
<p>Control: Reconciled with the Accountant</p>
<p>Escalate: City Accountant</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th>4. Estimate costs minimised</th>
<th>M&amp;E unit with sector offices</th>
<th><p>Estimate economic and social costs minimised, with method and assumptions stated.</p>
<p>Decision: Method stated and repeatable?</p></th>
<th><p>In: PDRA scenario; post-event data</p>
<p>Out: Costs-minimised section</p></th>
<th><p>Time: Within 30 days</p>
<p>Control: Estimates labelled as estimates</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMO Head</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th>5. Review and sign</th>
<th>CDRRMO Head; City Mayor</th>
<th><p>Review the report (Annex 7-D outline); the Mayor signs.</p>
<p>Decision: Complete?</p></th>
<th><p>In: Draft</p>
<p>Out: Signed report; GOV-F13</p></th>
<th><p>Time: Within 40 days</p>
<p>Control: Second reader checks figures</p>
<p>Escalate: City Mayor</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="header">
<th>6. Submit</th>
<th>CDRRMO Head</th>
<th><p>Submit by the confirmed route; record the reference and date on GOV-F13.</p>
<p>Decision: Submitted by day 45?</p></th>
<th><p>In: Signed report</p>
<p>Out: Submission proof</p></th>
<th><p>Time: By day 45</p>
<p>Control: Late submission reported to the CDRRMC</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMC</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<th>7. Learn</th>
<th>M&amp;E unit</th>
<th><p>Feed findings into the AAR (SOP 7-04) and CAPA register; update the event and loss database.</p>
<p>Decision: Lessons recorded?</p></th>
<th><p>In: Report</p>
<p>Out: ME-F05; ME-F07 entries</p></th>
<th><p>Time: Within 15 days of submission</p>
<p>Control: Linked to the report</p>
<p>Escalate: CDRRMO Head</p></th>
</tr>
</thead>

</tbody>

## 15. Responsibility Assignment (RACI)

| **\[R\] Responsible** | **\[A\] Accountable** | **\[C\] Consulted** | **\[I\] Informed** |
|-----------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|--------------------|

"A" is the single proposed process-accountable owner; "R" performs; "C" is consulted; "I" is informed. The RACI allocates work; it does not transfer legal powers.

**Table 7.32**

*RACI for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning*

| **Activity**                           | **CC** | **MY** | **HD** | **ME** | **TWG** | **EOC** | **AS** | **VA** | **DPO** | **ACC** |
|----------------------------------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|---------|---------|--------|--------|---------|---------|
| LDRRMP indicator set and annual report | A      | I      | R      | R      | R       | I       | –      | –      | C       | C       |
| IAT fieldwork and scoring              | I      | –      | A      | R      | C       | C       | R      | –      | C       | –       |
| IAT validation and release             | I      | –      | A      | R      | C       | C       | C      | R      | –       | –       |
| After-action review                    | I      | I      | A      | R      | C       | R       | –      | –      | –       | –       |
| CAPA register                          | C      | I      | A      | R      | R       | R       | –      | –      | –       | C       |
| 45-day post-declaration report         | I      | A      | R      | R      | C       | R       | –      | –      | –       | R       |
| Event and loss database                | I      | –      | A      | R      | C       | C       | –      | –      | C       | –       |
| Lessons and Manual revision            | C      | I      | A      | R      | C       | C       | –      | –      | –       | –       |
| Data protection and breach response    | I      | A      | R      | C      | I       | C       | –      | –      | R       | –       |

*Note. CC = CDRRMC; MY = City Mayor; HD = CDRRMO Head; ME = M&E unit (CDRRMO Research and Planning); TWG = CDRRMP Technical Working Group focal offices; EOC = EOC Manager and staff; AS = assessors; VA = validators; DPO = City Data Protection Officer; ACC = City Accountant. For data protection, the Mayor is accountable as head of the personal information controller, acting through the DPO.*

| 5       | Recovery, Rehabilitation and Build Back Better                            | Sends recovery monitoring and closeout lessons; receives PDNA data back through the database.                                                    |
| 6       | DRRM Financing, Resource Management and Accountability                    | Sends utilisation reports and COA findings; receives corrective actions on funds, stocks and inventory.                                          |
| 8       | Stakeholder Engagement and Institutional Partnerships                     | Manages the networks whose exchanges this chapter records.                                                                                       |
| 9       | Public Awareness, Community Resilience and Capacity Development           | Runs the exercise programme that this chapter evaluates; delivers training actions from the CAPA register.                                       |
| 10      | Institutional Sustainability, Deep Resilience and Recognition             | Uses IAT results, AARs and the CAPA record as evidence for recognition systems and the improvement agenda.                                       |

## 20. Concluding Notes

The City has the pieces of a learning system: a results-based M&E design in its 10-Year Plan, a Council with the duty to monitor, a working group with thematic focal offices, regular reports to OCD and the DILG, and now a full institutional baseline. What it lacks is the loop that ties them together: one register, one calendar, one database, and the habit of closing an action only when it has worked.

Writing these procedures does not implement them. Until the first annual results report has been presented, the first validated IAT cycle has fed the CAPA register, one event or exercise has gone through an AAR to verified closure, and the 45-day report template has been agreed with OCD VIII, this chapter remains a controlled working draft.

**CHAPTER 8**

# Stakeholder Engagement and Institutional Partnerships

| **Chapter at a Glance** |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| What this chapter does  | Organises work with partners: the partner register, mutual aid with other LGUs, augmentation from the Province and national agencies, Part C interface agreements, utilities, and CSO, private-sector and academe seats on the CDRRMC. |
| Main procedures         | SOP 8-01 to 8-08                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Read with               | Chapters 1, 4 and 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Status                  | Draft 1.0, 12 November 2026. Working draft for validation (workshop 1–4 December 2026); not approved.                                                                                                                                  |

> READING NOTE. A partnership allocates work; it does not transfer legal authority. Every office, agency, utility, LGU and organisation named in this chapter keeps its own mandate, chain of command and accountability. No agreement under this chapter binds the City until the Sangguniang Panlungsod has authorised it and the City Mayor has signed it (RA 7160 Sec. 22(c)).

## 1. Introduction and Assessment-Informed Rationale

No city manages disaster risk alone. In Ormoc, the decisions that most change risk are made outside the CDRRMO: where the CPDO allows development, whether the Building Official has checked an evacuation centre, how fast LEYECO V restores power to the hospital, whether the schools can keep teaching, whether a neighbouring town can lend a rescue team when every Ormoc team is deployed. Chapters 1 to 7 set what the CDRRMO and the EOC do. This chapter sets how they work with everyone else, before, during and after an event.

The chapter covers two kinds of relationship. The first is **external**: with the Province, the region and national agencies; with neighbouring LGUs; and with CSOs, volunteer groups, the private sector, utilities, academe, faith-based groups and communities (Figure 8.1). The second is the **interface** with other City offices that own systems on which disaster risk depends. The IAT measures this second kind separately, in Part C, and this chapter is its home in the Manual.

**Figure 8.1**

*The City's DRRM Stakeholder Ecosystem*

The baseline shows a City that helps others and works with many partners, but mostly event by event and without standing agreements (Table 8.1). Partnerships with CSOs, the private sector and academe are documented and in use (A10.2, score 3). There is no reciprocal mutual aid agreement with any neighbouring LGU (A10.1, score 1), although the City has sent cash and rice to LGUs in Leyte, Southern Leyte, Cebu, Mindanao and Batangas after their disasters. Part C, the interface with other City offices, has an Interface Index of **1.41 (Initial)**, with two High gaps: the structural safety of the EOC, evacuation centres and critical facilities (C2.1) and health anticipatory action (C4.1) (Figure 8.2).

### 1.1 What the Records Show

- **Helping neighbours, without an agreement.** After Typhoon Odette the CDRRMC and the SP sent cash to five Southern Leyte LGUs, five Leyte LGUs, Cebu City and the Province of Cebu (CDRRMC Res. Nos. 12, 14 and 15, s. 2021; SP Res. Nos. 2021-365, -367 and -369, the first authorising PHP 11.24 million from the 2021 QRF) and donated rice (SP Res. No. 2021-368). Earlier resolutions assisted LGUs hit by the Mindanao earthquakes (2019) and the Taal eruption (2020). CDRRMC Res. No. 13, s. 2021 adopted Proclamation No. 1267 so that the City could use its LDRRMF to assist other affected LGUs. None of these created a reciprocal arrangement.

- **Partnerships that exist.** SP Res. No. 2021-036 authorised the MOA among the City, the National Resilience Council, the Carlos P. Romulo Foundation and EDC. SP Res. No. 2021-357 authorised an MOU with the Oscar M. Lopez Center for climate and geo-hazard research and training. SP Res. No. 2023-347 authorised the MOA with the CPR-RIMT Rapid Rescue Rider Ormoc Chapter for volunteer augmentation of HEMS and the CDRRMO (the annexed copy is unsigned). CDRRMC Res. No. 04, s. 2025 created an Education Resilience and DRRM Coordination Group with all tertiary institutions.

- **Working groups with partners.** EO 2023-0025 (CDRA Technical Working Group, with LEYECO V and NGCP among partners); EO 2023-0026 (Project TRANSFORM Technical Working Group with DENR, EDC and the NRC under the Adopt-a-City programme); EO 2023-0042 (El Niño Task Force, including CPR-RIMT and two farmers' cooperatives); the City CCCM Team EO of 2022 (CSWDO-led, with the Red Cross, an NGO and a civic group; the EO number is to be confirmed).

- **Council seats.** EO 2024-032A gives the CDRRMC five CSO seats and two private-sector seats (EDC Leyte Geothermal and LEYECO V); a third private-sector seat is blank. The academe seat of the earlier EO was dropped; CDRRMC Res. No. 10, s. 2024 recommends the City College of Ormoc as a regular member, with no amending EO yet.

- **Volunteers.** CDRRMC Res. No. 07, s. 2024 approves the accreditation of community disaster volunteers under RA 10121 Sec. 13, and Res. Nos. 03 and 04, s. 2022 cover their guidelines and insurance. Ordinance No. 160, s. 2024 institutionalises the City volunteer programme.

- **Utilities, event by event.** CDRRMC Res. No. 10, s. 2021 asked LEYECO V to run its 2 MW standby generator at Barangay Alta Vista during the Odette outage. There is no standing restoration-priority arrangement with power, water or telecom providers (C2.2).

### 1.2 Design Considerations

1.  **Mandates stay with their owners.** Agreements set who does what and how to ask; they never move command, legal powers or accountability.

2.  **Agree before the event.** A partner who has signed, been briefed and been tested in a drill can be called in minutes; a partner who has not is a hope.

3.  **Technical, reciprocal and apolitical.** Mutual aid is framed as an exchange between technical offices for defined resources, activated by request and governed by the host LGU's command, so that it survives changes in leadership.

4.  **One register.** Every agreement, its term, its focal person and its review date sit in one partner register, so that lapsed or unsigned agreements are seen and not counted.

5.  **Interfaces are owned elsewhere.** For Part C, the lead office owns the indicator and the work; the CDRRMO coordinates, supplies risk information and reports. This chapter sets the interface, not the technical content, which stays in Chapters 3 to 6.

6.  **Inclusion and accountability.** Groups that represent women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities and other at-risk people are partners, not only beneficiaries, and communities have a way to raise concerns.

## 2. Purpose and Intended Results

This chapter sets how the City identifies, agrees, authorises, registers, exercises, activates and reviews its DRRM relationships with other governments, organisations and City offices.

Intended results:

1.  A partner register lists every DRRM agreement with its legal authority, term, focal persons, roles before and after events, and review date (A10.2).

2.  Technical mutual aid agreements are in force with Kananga, Albuera, Merida and Isabel and, where possible, the Province of Leyte (A10.1).

3.  Each Part C lead office has an interface agreement naming its focal person, the actions it owns and how it reports, and the Interface Index rises from its baseline (MR-17).

4.  Requests for augmentation follow the vertical route of the national response system, and incoming teams are received, briefed, tasked and demobilised in order.

5.  Power, water and telecom providers have standing restoration-priority arrangements (C2.2).

6.  The CDRRMC has its full membership, with SP-accredited CSOs, all private-sector seats filled and an academe seat (A1.2).

7.  Partners meet at least once a year before the typhoon season, and their commitments are recorded in the Chapter 6 resource inventory (B6.6).

8.  Assistance to other LGUs follows a lawful, documented route.

## 3. Scope, Application and Institutional Boundaries

**In scope:** vertical coordination with the Province, the region and national agencies; horizontal mutual aid with other LGUs; partnerships with CSOs, volunteer groups, the private sector, utilities, academe, faith-based groups, development partners and networks; interface arrangements with Part C lead offices; partner membership of the CDRRMC and the response clusters; partner engagement in planning, exercises and reviews; assistance to other LGUs.

## 5. Systems Thinking and Partnership Principles

Partnerships fail in predictable ways. A partner is called only during events, so neither side knows the other's capacity; agreements are signed by one administration and forgotten by the next; the same few organisations are asked every time while others drift away. These are feedback problems: engagement that happens only under pressure builds little trust, and low trust makes the next request slower. The remedy is steady engagement between events, so that trust and readiness accumulate.

- **Relationships before resources.** Meet partners before the season, exercise with them, and review with them after events. The annual partner forum (SOP 8-07) is the main mechanism.

- **Reciprocity.** Mutual aid that only flows one way is charity; agreements state what each side can offer and how costs are settled.

- **Institutional, not personal.** Agreements name positions and offices, not persons, and survive changes in leadership.

- **Clear interfaces.** Every interface names who leads, who supports and who decides, so that partners do not wait for each other.

- **Accountability to affected people.** Partners working with affected communities follow the same feedback and protection rules as City offices (Chapter 5, SOP 5-08).

## 6. Interface Governance With City Offices (Part C)

### 6.1 Principle

Part C of the IAT measures systems that reduce or manage disaster risk but sit outside the CDRRMO: land use and investment planning, building safety, lifelines, ecosystems, sector anticipatory actions and business continuity. Each indicator names a lead office. The lead office owns the indicator, the work and the evidence. The CDRRMO coordinates, supplies hazard and risk information, convenes the annual interface review and reports the Interface Index to the CDRRMC. The Interface Index is never added to the IMI, so a weak interface cannot be hidden by a strong CDRRMO score, or the reverse.

### 6.3 Interface Agreements and the Annual Review

Each lead office signs an interface agreement with the CDRRMO (PTN-F04): a joint office order or memorandum of understanding between City offices, approved by the City Administrator, or included in an executive order where the Mayor prefers. It names the focal person by position, the Part C indicators the office owns, the actions it will take in the year, the information the CDRRMO will give it, and how it reports. Once a year, before the IAT cycle, the CDRRMO convenes the lead offices for an interface review (SOP 8-04): each office presents its evidence, the Interface Index is computed, and gaps go to the CAPA register (Chapter 7). In MODE, the indicator_lead_offices table links each Part C indicator to its lead office, so the lead office's focal person sees and scores its own items.

## 7. Vertical Coordination: Province, Region and National Agencies

The City is part of the national DRRM system. Its CDRRMC sits under the Provincial DRRMC of Leyte and the RDRRMC VIII, and many national agencies have offices and assets in or near the City. Most of them already sit on the CDRRMC (EO 2024-032A).

| RDRRMC VIII and OCD Region VIII                                        | Regional coordination; RA 12287 request and reply; reports, including the 45-day report; technical assistance and trainings; PDNA support. | Chapter 1 (GOV-05); Chapter 7 (SOP 7-06); SOP 8-03 |
| DILG Region VIII and City Office                                       | Reporting templates and cut-off times; Operation L!sto; SGLG; local governance advice; CDRRMC member.                                      | Chapters 4, 7 and 10                               |
| DSWD Field Office VIII                                                 | Family food packs and non-food item augmentation; DROMIC reporting; CCCM standards.                                                        | Chapters 4 and 6                                   |
